findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the live conflict test guarantees BOTH the rebar-side and Jira-side edits are visible to the subsequent reconcile pass (e.g. read-back/poll each field until the written value is observed before running the pass), so remote != baseline is genuinely true when the conflict-alert assertion runs.
evidence: Plan: 'make a rebar-side edit to the description AND a Jira-side edit to the same field before the next pass; assert the next pass emits rebar's body (local-wins) and records the deduped outbound-field-conflict'
outbound_field_diff.py:457-464 fires the conflict only when not _remote_matches_baseline — i.e. only if the Jira-side edit is actually observed as remote != baseline at pass time
Live DC is a real Dockerized instance (tests/external/live_jira_dc/), where a write may not be immediately readable
findings.finding: The both-sides concurrent-edit scenario runs against a live Jira instance and assumes the next reconcile pass observes BOTH the rebar-side and the Jira-side edit before it computes the diff, but Jira DC read-after-write / field-indexing latency can make a just-written value not yet visible to the pass's fetch. If the Jira-side edit has not landed/propagated when the pass reads remote, remote==baseline and the both-sides conflict branch (outbound_field_diff.py:457-464) does not fire, silently turning the asserted local-wins + outbound-field-conflict outcome into a false pass or a flake. The plan does not specify a settle/confirm step ensuring both edits are visible to the pass.
findings.location: Approach (both-sides concurrent edit) / Testing (Live conflict) / AC line 2
scenarios: Jira-side description edit is accepted but not yet reflected in the field read the pass performs, so remote==baseline and no conflict alert is emitted despite a real both-sides divergence
Second-pass echo check reads a stale value and mis-attributes a re-push (or its absence)

search_files over tests/external/live_jira_dc for 'rendered' and 'expand=' returns (no matches) — the harness has never exercised this expand, so its DC 8.17.1 behavior is unprobed in-repo.

tests/fixtures/jira/search.json shows `"renderedFields": null` in captured payloads — evidence the expand can return null depending on request shape/platform; a Partially-verified signal that description-level HTML rendering on DC is not guaranteed.

conftest.py:111 `_request(path, ...)` takes an arbitrary path incl. query string, so issuing the expand is mechanically feasible (endpoint/param surface EXISTS on REST v2); it is the FIELD-level rendered output on DC 8.17.1 that is UNVERIFIED.
The plan itself states the DC wiki renderer 'cannot be modeled offline' — i.e. the rendered-HTML shape is exactly the unknown this test relies on and must therefore establish, not assume.
findings.finding: The story's load-bearing NEW external capability — that DC 8.17.1's `GET issue?expand=renderedFields` returns populated rendered HTML for the `description` field (bold/heading/code-macro) — is asserted but not verified; the repo has no prior `renderedFields` use on this harness and the only captured `renderedFields` payloads are Cloud fixtures where the value is `null`.
findings.location: Approach section, first bullet ('asserts rendered HTML through `?expand=renderedFields`') and AC line 1
scenarios: The pushed body lands but `renderedFields.description` comes back null/empty (or nested differently) on DC 8.17.1, so the HTML assertion has nothing to match and the test fails at its core oracle for a platform reason rather than a codec defect.
The wiki markup renders to HTML tags the assertion did not anticipate (e.g. `{code}` -> a specific macro DOM), making the markup-substring checks brittle.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit capability-probe step to the Approach/Testing sections: on the live instance, push a known wiki body via `rebar.edit_ticket`, GET `/rest/api/2/issue/{key}?expand=renderedFields`, and record the exact `renderedFields.description` HTML (confirming it is non-null and carries `<b>`/heading/code-macro markup on DC 8.17.1). Gate the HTML-substring assertions on that observed shape, and skip-with-reason (like the existing `_epic_link_field_id is None` SETUP-FAILED pattern) if the platform returns null rather than reporting it as a bridge defect.
